correctness.rationale: For every n≥3 and k≥1, a direct three-turn strategy wins when all responses have length at most n−3; an explicit invariant tracks two separate tokens {0,j} through a legal response of length at most n−2 when k≥n−1. These quantified arguments are supplemented by independently coded complete finite subset games for 60 parameter pairs, not replaced by enumeration. value.rationale: Alphabet-minimality is a natural missing dimension of a recently proved strict hierarchy. The theorem settles that exact minimum for every level, supplies a uniform two-letter witness and an exact winning cutoff, and determines sharp three-turn winning complexity and a memoryless losing invariant. This is structurally meaningful beyond a routine corollary of three-letter strictness, because restricting both opponents is nonmonotone.
